source_text:
Fragmentum in epistulam ad Philemonem (in catenis)
Phm
1,1 Ἐν πολλαῖς ἐπιστολαῖς ξένον τίθησι ῥῆμα τοῦ μέλλοντος εἰσάγεσθαι λόγου
κατασκευαστικόν, καὶ νῦν ἐπειδὴ ἔμελλεν ἀξιοῦν ὑπὲρ Ὀνησίμου τῇ ἑαυτοῦ ἀξίᾳ–
ἀξία δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸ δεδέσθαι–, τὸ ἀξιόπιστον τῆς παρακλήσεως δείκνυσιν.
thought_title: Paul's unusual word prepares his appeal
orientation: Photius is commenting on Philemon 1:1, explaining how Paul's opening word prepares for his request on behalf of Onesimus.
pass_a_gloss: In many letters he places an unusual word preparatory of the argument about to be introduced, and now since he was about to make a request on behalf of Onesimus by his own standing—and his standing is being in chains—he shows the credibility of the appeal.

choices.why: Keeps the word order and the literal force of τίθημι as placing; ξένον rendered as unusual per glossary.

choices.english: preparatory of the argument about to be introduced
choices.why: κατασκευαστικόν rendered as preparatory per glossary; the genitive phrase keeps the literal relation to the argument.
rejected: constructive of the argument to be introduced

choices.why: ἀξία rendered as standing per glossary; dative kept as instrumental by.
Glossary rendering; keeps the perfect passive infinitive as a state.
Both terms per glossary; keeps the genitive relation literal.

bible_refs.note: The fragment comments on Philemon 1:1, where Paul opens with his self-designation as a prisoner.

pass_b_english: Photius observes that in many letters Paul places an unusual word as preparation for the argument he is about to introduce. Here too, since he was about to make a request on behalf of Onesimus, he does so on the basis of his own standing—and his standing is being in chains. In this way Paul shows the credibility of his appeal.

last_rejected.fix: as preparatory for the argument he is about to introduce
last_rejected.ruling: κατασκευαστικόν means 'preparatory'; 'preparation' conveys same sense, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'was about to request/appeal', not 'does so'.
last_rejected.fix: he was about to make a request on behalf of Onesimus on the basis of his own standing
last_rejected.ruling: ἔμελλεν ἀξιοῦν = 'was about to request'; 'he does so' refers back, not mistranslation of ἀξιοῦν.

problems.quote: In this way he shows the credibility of his appeal
problems.why: Ambiguous whether 'he' is Paul or Photius; section break from intro loses attribution.
problems.fix: Specify 'Paul shows' or 'Photius observes that Paul shows'.

problems.quote: In many letters Paul places an unusual word
problems.why: Reader cannot tell if this is Photius's own observation or a paraphrase of a source; no attribution is given.
problems.fix: Clarify that this is Photius's own interpretive observation about Paul's letter-opening style.

edits.old: In many letters Paul places an unusual word
edits.new: Photius observes that in many letters Paul places an unusual word

edits.old: In this way he shows the credibility of his appeal.
edits.new: In this way Paul shows the credibility of his appeal.

fixed: Added 'Photius observes that' to clarify the observation is Photius's own.
Changed 'he' to 'Paul' to remove ambiguity about who shows the credibility.
